text:
Maya: onboarding nebulon-6b int4 - seeing weird hyphenation and extra spaces in short summaries. minimal repro below. anyone seen this pattern?

Theo: paste repro + sample outputs pls.

Maya: repro:
```bash
python ./eval_short.py --model nebulon-6b --quant int4 --prompt \"Key takeaway: model performed well\" --seed 3
```
FP16 -> \"Key takeaway: model performed well.\"
INT4 -> \"Key takeaway : model performed - well .\"
(Notice extra space before colon, stray hyphen inserted)

Luis: sounds like tokenizer remapping or a placeholder token sneaking in. Did conversion use an id-shift? Check conversion log for `--shift-vocab` flag. :mag_right: 

Maya: conversion log excerpt shows `--insert-reserved 60000` used. I didn't expect that.

bench-bot: perf snapshot: int4 nebulon-6b ~44ms/token, ppl +0.7 vs fp16 on news-mini.

Theo: high reserved id can change KV alignment and cause rotary phase aliasing for tokens with id > vocab_size_mod. Try re-running `scripts/strip_reserved.py --model nebulon-6b` and re-convert with `--preserve-ids`. Also run `python -c \"from transformers import AutoTokenizer as T; print(T.from_pretrained('nebulon-6b').encode(':'))\"` to confirm token ids.

QA-Lee: also run `scripts/compare_spans.py --fp16 runA --int4 runB --pattern \"\w+\b\"` to check whether token boundary changes explain punctuation spacing. If boundaries match, it's probably logit redistribution.

Maya: thanks - will strip reserved and re-run. filing ticket NB-2042 and tagging @Theo @Luis. Will update with diffs.
